paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when the pain is real, take it to the LORD. Jeremiah found out the people of his own hometown were plotting against him, and he didn't make a plan of his own. He said, "for to You I have committed my cause" (Jeremiah 11:20). Then the LORD answered him, and Jeremiah didn't have to carry it alone (Jeremiah 11:21-23).

Now watch what Jeremiah does next, because I LOVE this. He doesn't tidy up his words. He says, "Yet about Your judgments I wish to contend with You: Why does the way of the wicked prosper?" (Jeremiah 12:1). He asks the hard question straight to the LORD, and he starts with "Righteous are You, O LORD" (Jeremiah 12:1). I think that's the kind of honesty the LORD wants from you, friend, so bring Him the real question and not the polished one.

The LORD's answer to Jeremiah isn't a pat on the head. He tells him, "If you stumble in a peaceful land, how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?" (Jeremiah 12:5). I think the LORD is saying this road is going to get harder before it gets easier. So when it feels unfair and the faithful are the ones hurting, keep going, and keep bringing it to Him. The story isn't over for Jeremiah, and I wouldn't bet against the LORD, because I once lay in the dark of a junk drawer and He still reached in and called my name.
